thought.text: The naming context exists but no entries were loaded — the ldif didn't get added. Let me check the full bootstrap log to see what happened with the custom ldif.

reasoning_content:
The naming context dc=example,dc=org exists. However, even when I try to search with -b "dc=example,dc=org", I get "No such object" (32) returned. This is strange. A base scope search also returned "result: 32 No such object".

Wait a moment, actually, the base search returned "search: 2" (success), but there was no entry. Let me re-read:

```
# search result
search: 2
```
This is "success" (resultCode 0). Actually, in the first command, a base scope search against "dc=example,dc=org" returned "search: 2" and an entry? No, there was no entry. Hmm, the output only showed the extended LDIF header and search: 2. There was no actual entry, meaning the base entry doesn't exist.

But namingContexts indicates that dc=example,dc=org is a naming context. In other words, the database exists (the suffix is configured), but the base entry itself and the user entries have not been added.

So that means the ldif wasn't loaded. Let me check the openldap logs more thoroughly to see whether "Add custom bootstrap ldif" was actually executed and whether ldapadd succeeded. The grep for "ldapadd" didn't find anything. Let me look at the complete logs of the startup that succeeded.

Actually, this is the important problem: the test users were not loaded. The guide states that "these are automatically loaded on the first startup of the LDAP container." Let me check the logs to see what happened with the ldif processing.

Let me get the complete logs around the bootstrap.
